look_here_first: Use the whole plant first: a dry-limestone shrub or small multi-stemmed tree, commonly a low thicket. Then inspect bud, mature leaf underside, and ripe acorn cup—the cup scales are flattened, NOT strongly tuberculate. Leaf outline alone is unreliable.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Shrub or small tree usually to about 3–5 m, often forming thickets with multiple trunks near ground level.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Gray to light brown, flaky to papery and exfoliating.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Highly variable, from nearly entire to irregularly toothed or sinuately lobed; underside often has minute appressed stellate hairs.

key_traits.label: Acorn
key_traits.text: Cup saucer-shaped to shallowly cup-shaped, generally enclosing only about 1/8–1/4 of the nut.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: FNA variety: commonly 0.5–3(–5) m and multi-stemmed; adult leaf blade typically 30–60 × 20–40 mm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Q. sinuata leaf undersides vary from silvery minute appressed stellate hairs to nearly hairless, especially in shade leaves. Do not use apparent hairlessness as a species exclusion.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: FNA species-level twigs about 1–2(–3) mm, mostly glabrous; buds ovoid, 2–3 mm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorn nut 7–12(–15) mm long; shallow saucer cup about 3–8 mm deep × 8–12 mm broad (varietal description), commonly enclosing around 1/4 nut or less; scales flat and closely appressed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Plants along streams can approach intermediates with Q. sinuata var. sinuata; require habit, environment, and multiple organs before assigning variety.
